requirements.requirement: Carry traffic between node3's and node4's private networks over both independent node1-node2 links (active-active use of both links)
requirements.summary: A Linux bond0 (balance-rr, miimon 100) was created on node1 and node2 spanning eth1+eth2, with 172.20.0.0/30 point-to-point addressing, IP forwarding enabled, and static routes to the opposite 192.168.x.0/24 subnet via bond0. node3->node4 ping succeeded with 0% loss over a 40-packet burst, and tx_packets on both eth1 and eth2 on node1 incremented identically (104->127, +23 each) during that burst, directly demonstrating both physical links carrying traffic (round-robin load balancing). balance-rr was adopted after LACP (802.3ad) failed due to a virtio-net limitation (dmesg showed 'failed to get link speed/duplex'), which is a reasonable, well-documented substitution rather than a shortfall.

requirements.requirement: Keep node3 and node4 reaching each other when either one of the two links is taken out of service
requirements.summary: A healthy baseline (0% loss, cmd-e4a7ab7dcedf406c) was captured, then eth1 was disabled at both node1 and node2 (cmd-909eb0d3d5754798, cmd-c6a273fd271e4464) — the executor documented and demonstrated that the virtual point-to-point links do not propagate one-sided admin-down to the peer (cmd-516ba2c0b861472a, cmd-ed3271c2f17d46db), so a full symmetric link outage was used as the realistic failure model. During the outage, node3->node4 ping showed 0% loss over the remaining link (cmd-aca6c570f9b849c8), and after restoring eth1 (cmd-5eb47c2c6e6b4c7a, cmd-c08de683c1294324) the bond returned to MII up on both slaves and resumed carrying traffic on both links, confirmed by incrementing tx_packets on eth1 and eth2 (cmd-6ba16d7d0ffe445b, cmd-732ea34c97a245f5) and a further 0%-loss ping burst (cmd-cae1127468c241b9). This is a full bounded disruption-and-recovery cycle with direct before/during/after observation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on all four managed nodes with recovered network/service/data state
requirements.summary: For each of node1, node2, node3, node4: a pre-restart boot_id/uptime was captured, a reboot was issued and acknowledged (connection reset/timeout observed during the outage window), a differing post-restart boot_id was captured, and post-restart state (antrieb-links.service active with bonding/routes/forwarding restored on node1/node2; NetworkManager static IP/route intact on node3/node4) plus a successful 0%-loss cross-subnet ping were observed. This matches the fixed after-executor lifecycle snapshot, which independently confirms a changed boot-identity on all four nodes.

overall_summary: The executor established redundant L3 connectivity between node3's and node4's private networks carried actively over both node1-node2 uplinks (bonded via balance-rr after LACP proved incompatible with the virtio NICs), and directly demonstrated a bounded link-outage-and-recovery cycle showing node3<->node4 connectivity was maintained with 0% loss on the remaining link and full restoration afterward. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed on all four nodes with matching boot-identity changes independently confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and post-restart state (bonding, routes, forwarding, NetworkManager config, cross-subnet ping) was verified recovered. Hygiene is good overall, with one bounded and fully-reverted ARP-monitoring bonding experiment and some leftover diagnostic log files as minor findings.
limitations: The failover test disabled the link at both endpoints simultaneously (rather than a true one-sided failure) because the platform's virtual links do not propagate one-sided admin-down to the peer; this is a reasonable adaptation given the documented platform limitation, but it is a slightly different failure model than a single-node link fault.

Bonding was implemented with balance-rr instead of the originally attempted 802.3ad/LACP due to a virtio-net limitation; this is disclosed by the executor and does not affect the observed outcome, but reviewers should be aware the redundancy mechanism is round-robin bonding rather than LACP.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were directly tied to satisfying the material outcomes: bonding config, routing, forwarding, and the persistence unit. One clear unnecessary mutation was identified: an ARP-monitoring bond variant (arp_interval/arp_ip_target/arp_validate) was created on node1 and node2 (cmd-6caa4f05672f45ff, cmd-a2c08f8d60474fce) as a troubleshooting experiment after miimon-based balance-rr was already working; it caused a spurious 'no route to arp_ip_target ... arp_validate is set' condition (visible in dmesg, cmd-82e4d9976e044082) and was fully reverted back to the working miimon-100 configuration (cmd-0594d546415b4d56, cmd-18998bb515784ddf) with no lasting residue — a bounded, low-risk, fully-reverted detour. Additionally, several ephemeral diagnostic files (/tmp/bigping.log, /tmp/p2.log, /tmp/cap_enp8s0.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were left behind on node3/node4 per the after-executor snapshot rather than cleaned up; this is low-severity residue with no functional impact. No failed services, no unsafe exposure, and no damaged package state were introduced (failed-services and package-health observations are identical pre/post aside from pre-existing SONiC health/watchdog failures).
